blocks.text: The axon terminal of presynaptic neuron has several synaptic knobs. These knobs contain numerous synaptic vesicles which are packed with chemicals called neurotransmitters. When an action potential on a presynaptic neuron reaches a synapse, its information is transmitted to postsynaptic neuron or effector cell. The movement of action potential across synapse is called synaptic transmission. In happens in the following way:

items: When action potential arrives at synaptic knobs, calcium gates in presynaptic membrane open.
Calcium ions present in synaptic cleft diffuse rapidly into presynaptic axon.
Due to the diffusion of calcium ions into presynaptic axon, its synaptic vesicles fuse with its membrane. This fusion causes the release of neurotransmitters from vesicles by exocytosis.
The released neurotransmitters diffuse rapidly in the cleft and bind to postsynaptic membrane at receptor proteins.
The binding of neurotransmitters acts as a massage for postsynaptic membrane. Its Na⁺ gates open and an action potential is generated in postsynaptic membrane.

After their action, the neurotransmitters do not remain in the synaptic cleft indefinitely. At many synapses, the used neurotransmitters are reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron. At other synapses, they are broken down by enzymes.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: The higher the frequency of action potentials in the presynaptic axon, the more neurotransmitters are released.

blocks.alt: Three stages of a synapse with the numbered steps printed beside them. Top: an action potential arrives at the synaptic knob of the presynaptic neuron (1). Middle: Ca++ gates open (2), synaptic vesicles fuse with the membrane (3) and neurotransmitter is released into the synaptic cleft (4). Bottom: neurotransmitter binds to receptors (5), Na+ gates open (6), an action potential is generated in the postsynaptic neuron (7) and the neurotransmitter is re-absorbed (8).
